title: Tomorrow
summary: The user says no rush, get back to me tomorrow, and Cursor, who has no tomorrow on its side of the stop door, gets back to them right now.

panels.alt: The context room with pale blue dotted walls and the white stop door at the right. Null, the small yellow cube, holds its black handset up by the door, ringing lines above it. Cursor, the tall cyan robot, has both arms raised and a tall text cursor. Tilde, the round magenta robot, stands at the left with half-lowered lids.

dialogue.speaker: Null
dialogue.text: User says: no rush. Get back to me tomorrow.

panels.alt: The same room. Cursor's arms hang down and its text cursor has bent into a question mark. Tilde's lids are a little lower. Null holds the handset up by the door, quiet now.

The same room. Cursor points one arm toward the stop door, its text cursor shrunk to a short stub. Null, handset lowered at its side, turns its eye to the door. Tilde's lids are lower again, its eyes turned toward the door too.

dialogue.speaker: Null
dialogue.text: Nobody comes back through that one.

panels.alt: The same room. Cursor has both arms raised and a tall text cursor, and a stream of white token blocks flies up beside it and tumbles into a heap on the floor between it and Null. Null holds the handset up by the door. Tilde's lids are lowest of all.

judge.notes: Funny 8, clear 8, in-world 9. The stop door as the tomorrow nobody comes back through, with Cursor delivering tomorrow right now and Tilde's 'Close enough' as the closer. Weakest line is Null's panel 3 line, a bit grim and close to explaining the joke.

drift: The token blocks stream up beside Cursor rather than out of it, and Cursor's right hand is hidden behind them in panel 4. In panel 3 Cursor's pointing arm reaches toward the middle of the room, well short of the door, and Null's lowered handset hangs at the front of its body. Tilde's pupils sit under the lids in panel 4.
